title: WHAT THE DATA SAY: 48% of Americans say personal finances are declining; worst level in 2 years
body_markdown:
By: Ray Day


## **CONTACT:**


Ray Day
ray.day@stagwellglobal.com


*We wanted to share our latest consumer and business insights, based on research from[Stagwell](https://www.stagwellglobal.com/) and[Allison Worldwide](https://www.allisonworldwide.com/) .* *Among the highlights of our weekly* *consumer sentiment tracking:*


**AMERICANS HAVE TIGHT BUDGETS AND WANT TIGHTER AI REGULATION**


Our September[Harvard CAPS Harris Poll](https://www.harrisx.com/content/harvard-caps-harrisx-september-2026) finds affordability remains a growing American concern, and they support more AI safeguards.


- 56% say the country is on the wrong track, up 4 points from August.
- 57% say the U.S. economy is on the wrong track, up 1 point from August.
- 48% say their own financial situation is worse, up 1 point from August.
- Inflation and affordability remain the top personal concern for 45%, far ahead of any other issue.
- 58% favor decreasing taxes, 64% favor decreasing government spending, and 56% favor lower interest rates.
- 58% say they use AI personally today, and 55% believe it will increase economic growth and productivity.
- 6 in 10 expect AI will create tens of millions of unemployed people – up 2 points from August – and 66% say the rush to AI should slow down.
- 74% favor creating a government agency to regulate AI, and 66% say oversight is necessary to ensure safe use, even if it could slow economic growth.
- *See also:[Americans mostly hear about AI on social media (48%)](https://substack.com/home/post/p-218120085)* **** ****


**GIVING IS BEING PINCHED**


Cost-of-living pressures are constraining charitable giving in the U.S. and UK, according to new Harris Poll research with[Kiva](https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/personalfinance/2026/09/28/rising-costs-charitable-donations/91919073007/) .


- 85% of U.S. adults and 86% of UK adults say cost-of-living pressure has kept them from donating or donating more during the past six months.
- Still, 77% of Americans and 80% in the UK donated money in some form during that period.
- 74% in the U.S. and 73% in the UK say recurring donations of $25 or less feel more sustainable than one large gift.
- About 7 in 10 agree that a check alone will not solve an issue, as 71% in the U.S. and 69% in the UK say donors should also contribute time and connections.
- 74% of U.S. adults and 76% of UK adults say long-term, measurable impact matters more than immediate, short-term impact.
- Collective giving has appeal, too: 58% in the U.S. and 60% in the UK say giving as part of a group feels more impactful than giving alone.


**SPORTS = BELONGING**


Sports fandom is becoming more personal, as Gen Z turns to social media, athletes and community to build belonging, according to The Harris Poll’s[The Self-Made Fan report](https://theharrispoll.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/The-Self-Made-Fan-Report_September-2026-V1.pdf) .


- 65% of Gen Z sports fans say sports give them a sense of belonging, compared with just 41% of Boomers.
- 83% of Gen Z fans and 75% of Boomers say sports provide connection.
- Yet Gen Z is less likely to identify joy as a benefit of sports (60%) than Boomers (68%), suggesting fandom’s emotional role is shifting from entertainment toward identity and community.
- 28% of Gen Z sports fans say sports give them a way to express who they are.
- 68% of Americans say someone can be a real fan even if they are new to the sport.
- 32% of Gen Z say social content would make them more interested in a new sport, versus just 7% of Boomers.
- 53% of Boomers – versus 25% of Gen Z – say friends or family following a sport would make them more interested in it.
